L: Look, here are pictures of two interesting places in the US.
봐, 여기 미국의 흥미로운 장소 두 곳의 사진이 있어.
They look nice. If you go to the US, which of these places [would you like to] visit?
멋져 보인다. 만약 네가 미국에 간다면, 이 장소들 중 어느 곳을 방문하고 싶니?
[I'd like to] visit this place to see the famous statue and take pictures of the city.
나는 유명한 조각상을 보고 도시의 사진을 찍기 위해 이곳을 방문하고 싶어.
I agree! [I hope] I can go there one day.
나도 그렇게 생각해! 나는 언젠가 거기에 갈 수 있기를 바라.
I'm looking at pictures of Japan. I'm [going to] go there with my family.
나는 일본 사진을 보고 있어. 나는 가족과 함께 거기에 갈 거야.
That's great. What do you want to see there?
멋지다. 너는 거기서 무엇을 보고 싶니?
We want to see traditional places like the one in this picture. We're [planning to] stay in a traditional house, too.
우리는 이 사진에 있는 곳 같은 전통적인 장소들을 보고 싶어. 우리는 전통 가옥에도 머물 계획이야.
That sounds amazing! [I hope] I can go there someday.
굉장하다! 나도 언젠가 거기에 갈 수 있기를 바라.
I'm planning my trip to France.
That sounds exciting! What [would you like to] do there?
신나겠다! 너는 거기서 무엇을 하고 싶니?
[I'd like to] stay at a place by the ocean and spend some time at the beach.
나는 바닷가에 있는 곳에 머물면서 해변에서 시간을 좀 보내고 싶어.
Wow, the water looks bright blue in this picture.
와, 이 사진에서 물이 밝은 파란색으로 보여.
[I hope] you have a nice trip!
Where are you going to go?
I'm going to go to Rome.
What [would you like to] do there?
That sounds cool! [I hope] you enjoy your trip.
Dad, let's plan our trip to Australia!
Okay, Yumi. Where [would you like to] go?
그래, 유미야. 너는 어디에 가고 싶니?
[I'd like to] visit the Sydney Opera House.
저는 시드니 오페라 하우스를 방문하고 싶어요.
Then [how about] [taking a tour] of the Sydney Opera House on the first day? We can learn about the history of the building.
그럼 첫째 날에 시드니 오페라 하우스를 둘러보는 게 어떠니? 우리는 그 건물의 역사에 대해 배울 수 있어.
That sounds perfect! I'd like to watch a live performance, too.
완벽해요! 저는 라이브 공연도 보고 싶어요.
Of course! We can buy tickets to an opera or a classical music concert.
물론이지! 우리는 오페라나 클래식 음악 콘서트 표를 살 수 있어.
I want to see an opera.
Okay. I'll [look for] tickets to an opera.
Thank you, Dad. [I hope] we have a great time.
고마워요, 아빠. 우리가 즐거운 시간을 보내길 바라요.
Where [would you like to] travel to?
What would you like to do there?
I'd like to go to the Night Safari.
We're finally here, the lantern festival in Thailand!
우리가 드디어 여기 왔구나, 태국의 등불 축제에!
There are already a lot of people here.
Yes. I'm [excited to see] the bright lanterns in the sky.
그래. 나는 하늘에 있는 밝은 등불들을 볼 생각에 신나.
Me too! But why do people fly lanterns?
저도요! 그런데 사람들은 왜 등불을 날려요?
People [send away] bad luck with the lanterns and [make wishes].
사람들은 등불과 함께 불운을 쫓아 보내고 소원을 빈단다.
Yes. I bought a lantern for us, too. Let's [make a wish]!
그래. 내가 우리를 위한 등불도 하나 샀어. 소원을 빌자!
Okay. [I'd like to] [wish for] our family's happiness.
네. 저는 우리 가족의 행복을 빌고 싶어요.
That's a wonderful wish. Are you [ready to] fly our lantern? 3, 2, 1, go!
멋진 소원이구나. 우리 등불을 날릴 준비가 됐니? 3, 2, 1, 출발!
Wow, it's beautiful. [I really hope] our wish comes true.
와, 아름다워요. 저는 우리 소원이 이루어지길 정말 바라요.
I made a poster for the Rio Carnival.
It is held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, [from] late February [to] early March every year.
그것은 매년 2월 말부터 3월 초까지 브라질 리우데자네이루에서 열려.
I see. What [would you like to] do at the festival?
그렇구나. 너는 그 축제에서 무엇을 하고 싶니?
[I'd like to] see a parade and learn a traditional Brazilian dance.
나는 퍼레이드를 보고 브라질 전통 춤을 배우고 싶어.
This place in the magazine looks cool. It says it's a green tea field.
잡지에 있는 이곳은 멋져 보여. 녹차밭이라고 쓰여 있어.
Yeah. That's in Boseong. It [is famous for] green tea. I went there last May.
응. 그곳은 보성에 있어. 그곳은 녹차로 유명해. 나는 지난 5월에 거기에 갔어.
It was amazing. I went to the Green Tea Festival there! It [is held] every year.
굉장했어. 나는 거기서 녹차 축제에 갔어! 그것은 매년 열려.
What can I do at the festival?
그 축제에서는 무엇을 할 수 있니?
You can [pick] green tea leaves and [taste] green tea.
녹차 잎을 따고 녹차를 맛볼 수 있어.
That sounds fun! [I'd like to] go there, too.
[I hope] you can go there someday!
네가 언젠가 거기에 갈 수 있기를 바라!

lines: After a nine-hour flight, my family finally arrived at the international airport in Honolulu.
When we came through the gate, I heard someone calling my name.
My cousin Soobin and her family were waiting for us.
When we saw each other, we hugged and jumped together in a circle.
Then Soobin put a pretty flower necklace around my neck.
She called it a lei and said that “lei” means “warm welcome.”
We visited Diamond Head first.
It is a famous hiking place.
My uncle told us how it got its name.
In the past, people mistook its shiny rocks for diamonds.
So, they named the place Diamond Head.
How interesting!
The view from the top was amazing.
Soobin and I took many pictures there!
Today we went to a culture center.
We learned about traditional Hawaiian culture there.
First, we learned what some Hawaiian words mean.
“Aloha” is used to say “hello” or “goodbye,” and “mahalo” means “thank you.”
Then it was hula dance time!
Surprisingly, many of the movements stood for things in nature.
For example, if you raise your arms above your head in a circle, it stands for the moon.
When I danced hula, I could feel the Hawaiian people’s love for nature.
On the way back to Soobin’s house, we saw a big, beautiful rainbow.
Soobin explained, “You can often see rainbows in Hawaii.
So, Hawaii is called the Rainbow State.”
Today, we headed to Hanauma Bay to go snorkeling.
Before snorkeling, we watched an educational video.
We learned not to harm the sea animals or touch the coral.
The underwater world was wonderful.
We saw lots of colorful fish and a turtle swimming there.
It was amazing!
It is already the last day of our trip.
I’m sad to go home, but I will always remember Hawaii.
Aloha, Soobin! Mahalo, Hawaii!
